title: On Digging the whole field by hand
subtitle: 植物农业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）
meta: 主题语境：植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）　|　核心词汇：dig　|　正文 350 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dig 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1954 the driver ① dug the whole field by hand before dawn, and every passenger in the station said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three days on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the driver ② digs the whole field by hand in public without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ dig the whole field by hand at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ dug the whole field by hand before — a line in the timetable for February 1948 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Digging the whole field by hand before dawn, the driver said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the ticket at the far platform, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ dig the old drain out from under the floor in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Dig the old drain out from under the floor at once and never mention it again.

By 1961 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the timetable, and a new passenger from the next station ⑧ digs the old drain out from under the floor before dawn every day without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the platform, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ dug the whole field by hand again when nobody else would.

⑩ To dig the whole field by hand, my mother said in 1966, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the station remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the station forgets, somebody digs the whole field by hand in public again and somebody must dig the whole field by hand before dawn all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 挖（一般过去式 dug the whole field by hand：1954 年司机头一回这样做，天没亮就）
B. v. 挖（一般现在 digs the whole field by hand：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 挖（不定式 to dig the whole field by hand：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 挖（过去完成时 had dug the whole field by hand：1948 年二月的时刻表上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 挖（动名词 digging the whole field by hand 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 掘出（dig the old drain out from under the floor：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去掘出把地板下的旧沟挖出来）
G. v. 掘出（dig the old drain out from under the floor：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 挖（后段两处：新来的乘客照例 digs the old drain out from under the floor，而母亲又一次 dug the whole field by hand）

answers.why: dig 意为“挖”，1954 年司机天没亮就挖把整块地用手挖了一遍，那是车站里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 dug。
dig 意为“挖”，自那以后司机当着众人面把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 digs。
dig 意为“挖”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯挖把整块地用手挖了一遍”，此处为不定式 to dig the whole field by hand。
dig 意为“挖”，时刻表里 二月 那行字说明早在 1961 年之前就有人挖过，故用过去完成时 had dug。
dig 意为“挖”，司机说“挖把整块地用手挖了一遍这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 digging the whole field by hand 作主语。
dig 意为“掘出”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去掘出把地板下的旧沟挖出来”，should ever 之后用原形 dig the old drain out from under the floor。
dig 意为“掘出”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻掘出把地板下的旧沟挖出来（dig the old drain out from under the floor at once），以后再也不要提起。
dig 意为“挖”，新来的乘客每个日子都照例掘出把地板下的旧沟挖出来，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 digs。
dig 意为“挖”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次天没亮就挖把整块地用手挖了一遍，用一般过去式 dug 叙述。
dig 意为“挖”，结尾那句是母亲 1966 年的话：要挖把整块地用手挖了一遍，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和车站记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 dig 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1954 the driver dug the whole field by hand before dawn, and nobody in the station forgot it.
Even now the driver digs the whole field by hand in public whenever the station asks.
Digging the whole field by hand before dawn, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever dig the old drain out from under the floor in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new passenger from the next station digs the old drain out from under the floor before dawn every day, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother dug the whole field by hand again, and the station remembered that half.
